topic: Lambda Init Capture: Moving Non-Copyable Resources into Closure
explanation: Generalized lambda capture (C++14) allows the definition and initialization of new data members within the closure object using arbitrary expressions. This is critical for capturing variables that are non-copyable (e.g., `std::unique_ptr`, `std::thread`, `std::future`). By using `[ data_member = std::move(local_variable) ]`, the resource ownership is efficiently transferred into the closure, ensuring the lambda holds the resource directly.
practical_example: A developer needs a lambda to execute asynchronously using `std::async`. The lambda requires exclusive ownership of a large object. Generalized capture allows moving the `std::unique_ptr` holding the object into the lambda, preventing unnecessary copying and ensuring correct lifetime management.
book: Effective Modern C++ by Scott Meyers
